senses.sense_definition: A recurring theme, motif, or device in art, literature, or popular culture.

examples.text: The film relies on the familiar <w>trope</w> of a detective haunted by past mistakes.
Science fiction novels often use the <w>trope</w> of rebel factions fighting an oppressive empire.

senses.sense_definition: A figure of speech in which words or expressions are used in a nonliteral or figurative sense.

examples.text: Metaphor and irony are two kinds of <w>trope</w> studied in classical rhetoric.
The speaker employed a clever <w>trope</w> to make his political argument more memorable.

senses.sense_definition: An addition or embellishment of music or text inserted into a traditional church liturgy.

examples.text: Medieval singers introduced a poetic <w>trope</w> into the opening chant of the Mass.
Scholars trace the origins of liturgical drama back to an Easter <w>trope</w>.

senses.sense_definition: A tangent space that intersects a quartic surface along a conic section.

examples.text: The geometer demonstrated that the plane touches the quartic surface as a <w>trope</w>.
Each <w>trope</w> on the Kummer surface corresponds to a conic section counted twice.

senses.sense_definition: The reciprocal singularity of a node on a geometric surface.

examples.text: In dual projective geometry, each node is paired with a corresponding <w>trope</w>.
The algebraic equation accounts for every <w>trope</w> across the reciprocal surface.

senses.sense_definition: A short melodic phrase or cadence terminating a melody in early music.

examples.text: The musician avoided the expected cadence by ending with an unusual melodic <w>trope</w>.
Each musical <w>trope</w> served to smooth the transition between liturgical sections.

senses.sense_definition: In twelve-tone composition, a pair of complementary six-note chords containing all twelve tones.

examples.text: Hauer developed a modern compositional method organized around forty-four distinct hexachord <w>tropes</w>.
The composer transposed the primary <w>trope</w> to create variations throughout the movement.

senses.sense_definition: A musical cantillation pattern, or the notation symbol representing it, used in chanting scripture.

examples.text: The student spent weeks memorizing the traditional <w>trope</w> before chanting from the Torah scroll.
Every printed mark indicating the <w>trope</w> guides both the melody and grammatical phrasing.

senses.sense_definition: In ancient philosophical skepticism, one of several modes of argument used to suspend judgment.

examples.text: Sextus Empiricus described each skeptical <w>trope</w> as an antidote to dogmatic belief.
The fifth Pyrrhonian <w>trope</w> concerns the fallibility of human perception under varying conditions.

senses.sense_definition: An individual, unrepeatable instance of a property, as opposed to a universal attribute.

examples.text: In contemporary metaphysics, the distinct redness of this apple is regarded as an abstract <w>trope</w>.
Proponents of trope theory argue that every concrete object is merely a bundle of such <w>tropes</w>.

senses.sense_definition: To represent or treat something figuratively, symbolically, or as a recurring motif.

examples.text: The poet chose to <w>trope</w> political oppression as an unending winter season.
Critics observed how modern directors repeatedly <w>trope</w> technology as an existential menace.

senses.sense_definition: To embellish or expand a liturgical chant or text with added musical or poetic material.

examples.text: Monastic composers began to <w>trope</w> traditional hymns to enrich celebratory services.
By actively <w>troping</w> the solemn liturgy, medieval musicians laid the groundwork for liturgical drama.

senses.sense_definition: To coin or convert something into a cultural or literary trope.

examples.text: Online commentators quickly <w>troped</w> the celebrity scandal into a widespread cultural joke.
The satirist managed to <w>trope</w> corporate jargon into a vehicle for political commentary.

senses.sense_definition: To analyze or interpret a literary or artistic work through the study of its tropes.

examples.text: Scholars often <w>trope</w> classical tragedies to expose underlying ideological assumptions.
Her academic essay seeks to <w>trope</w> nineteenth-century gothic fiction from a feminist viewpoint.

senses.sense_definition: To think, express oneself, or write in figurative terms.

examples.text: Philosophers who constantly <w>trope</w> risk obscuring simple truths behind complex rhetoric.
He preferred to <w>trope</w> rather than deliver direct statements in his philosophical prose.
